description.text: FIS is a financial technology company providing solutions to financial institutions, businesses and developers. We unlock financial technology to the world across the money lifecycle underpinning the world's financial systems. Our people are dedicated to advancing the way the world pays, banks and invests, by helping our clients to confidently run, grow and protect their businesses. Our expertise comes from decades of experience helping financial institutions and businesses of all sizes adapt to meet the needs of their customers by harnessing where reliability meets innovation in financial technology. Headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida, FIS is a member of the Fortune 500® and the Standard & Poor’s 500® Index. FIS is incorporated under the laws of the State of Georgia as Fidelity National Information Services, Inc., and our stock is traded under the trading symbol "FIS" on the New York Stock Exchange.

analysis_md:
# FIS — Fidelity National Information Services, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-16. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Core banking, payments and capital-markets processing for financial institutions — mission-critical, multi-year, mostly recurring revenue. The company is mid portfolio-reset: it sold a 55% stake in Worldpay Merchant Solutions in February 2024, then on January 9, 2026 closed a linked swap — acquiring Global Payments' Issuer Solutions business (formerly TSYS, now FIS Total Issuing Solutions; $13.5B enterprise value, ~$7.7B cash plus its Worldpay stake) and selling its remaining 45% Worldpay stake to Global Payments (Worldpay at a $24.25B enterprise valuation). FIS is now the world's largest issuer processor (40B+ transactions/yr, clients in 75+ countries per the closing release) with no merchant-acquiring exposure. In scope: market cap $18.866B at $35.94 (key_numbers.md).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow (continuing operations) $2,608,000,000; capex $154,000,000; SBC $181,000,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $2,273,000,000 = $4.33/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $4.33, latest FY OE total $2.273B). OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years.
- Maintenance version FY2025: $4,096,000,000 (financials_history.csv) — rejected as the base: it is flattered by working-capital/discontinued-basis effects around the Worldpay separation, while the OCF-based conservative figure is cash and continuing-operations clean.
- History caveat (basis break, see Flags): OE/share printed $6.94 in 2023 on a total-company OCF basis and $3.41 in 2024 on a continuing-operations-only basis after Worldpay deconsolidation — the drop is the basis change, not a collapse of the continuing business. The 3-yr median and the latest FY coincide at $4.33/share.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $2,608,000,000 − prior YTD $839,000,000 + current YTD $1,207,000,000 = **TTM $2,976,000,000**
- Capex: FY $154,000,000 − prior YTD $76,000,000 + current YTD $76,000,000 = **TTM $154,000,000**
- SBC: FY $181,000,000 − prior YTD $96,000,000 + current YTD $101,000,000 = **TTM $186,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **517,000,000**
- **TTM OE total $2,636,000,000 → base OE/share $5.10** (base_source: ttm_json)
- Caveat on this base, stated plainly: the TTM is a hybrid — H2 2025 is pre-deal FIS (no Issuer Solutions), H1 2026 includes Issuer Solutions from the January 9, 2026 close. A full pro forma year would differ; management's pro forma FY2025 combined revenue was $13.186B with adjusted EBITDA of $5.431B (41.2% margin, per the deal 8-K), vs filed FY2025 revenue of $10.677B. The hybrid likely understates a clean post-deal run rate on revenue, but the deal's added interest cost is also not in the OE definition — confidence is set low partly for this.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, not wide
Justification: real switching costs in mission-critical core banking and issuer processing, but a decade of ROIC proxy below the cost of capital proves the stickiness has not converted into excess returns. ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json, roic_proxy series): 4.10% (2016), 6.01% (2017), 6.40% (2018), 1.07% (2019), 0.52% (2020), 1.25% (2021), 1.98% (2022), 2.93% (2023), 4.71% (2024), 5.11% (2025) — improving, still not above a plausible cost of capital in any of the last seven years. Gross margin: 33.2% (2016), 35.9% (2021), 37.2% (2023), 37.6% (2024), 36.9% (2025) — mid-30s and roughly flat, not the expanding margin of a pricing-power compounder.
- FOR: mission-critical core banking and issuer processing with high switching costs and multi-year recurring contracts; scale after the Issuer Solutions deal (largest global issuer processor, 40B+ transactions/yr, 75+ countries); recurring-revenue base (pro forma recurring revenue growth 4.8% in Q1 2026); integrated banking + issuing stack for large and super-regional banks smaller rivals cannot match.
- AGAINST: ROIC proxy below cost of capital for a decade (0.5–6.4%, 5.11% in 2025); Fiserv and Jack Henry competition (Jack Henry holds the community-bank niche at ~98% retention); bank consolidation shrinks the client base and cloud-native cores lower switching barriers; serial large M&A (Worldpay 2019, largely written down and exited 2024–26) destroyed capital and left high leverage.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-16)
Growth sanity check (mandatory): the engine blend is 4.56% (components, key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y −3.18%, rev CAGR 3y 3.18%, latest rev YoY 5.43%, OE/share CAGR 2y −20.99%). Every component straddles a basis break — the 5-yr CAGR and the OE/share CAGR are dragged by the Worldpay deconsolidation, not by continuing-business decline. Against actual prints: FY2025 filed revenue grew 5.43%; Q1 2026 GAAP revenue grew ~30% only because Issuer Solutions closed — pro forma growth was 6.5% (recurring 4.8%); full-year 2026 pro forma revenue guidance started at 5.1–5.7% and was cut to 4.5–5.0% in the Q2 2026 reporting (Capital Markets softness). The base start of 4.6% sits inside the guided range — kept. The default scenario offsets were NOT kept: the default super-bull start (16.6%) is more than 3x the top of pro forma guidance and no print supports it, and the default super-bear start (−7.4%) assumes a revenue collapse a recurring-revenue processor has not printed on a continuing basis. Offsets were recalibrated to −0.08 / −0.04 / 0.0 / +0.035 / +0.065, giving starts of −3.4% / 0.6% / 4.6% / 8.1% / 11.1% — the bull end now requires synergy delivery and share gains, not fantasy. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 and OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 are the defaults, kept: 35% on bear-or-worse reflects the leverage and the guidance cut. Price $35.94.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −3.4% | 0.75 | Integration stumbles, Capital Markets slide deepens, deleveraging eats all FCF | $24.46 | 10.80% |
| Bear | 25% | 0.6% | 0.90 | Pro forma growth stalls near zero; guidance cut was the start, not the end | $34.71 | 14.56% |
| Base | 30% | 4.6% | 1.00 | Guided 4.5–5.0% pro forma growth, normal fade over the CAP | $45.55 | 18.26% |
| Bull | 25% | 8.1% | 1.10 | Issuer synergies land, cross-sell into the banking base works | $57.92 | 22.10% |
| Super bull | 10% | 11.1% | 1.25 | Synergies plus buyback resumption compound OE/share at low double digits | $74.47 | 26.79% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $46.72 (+30.0% vs price), IV@12% $61.95 (+72.4%), IV@10% $78.92, weighted IRR 18.62%, base-case IRR 18.26%**
- **Tier by numbers: B.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 14.19%, terminal value 18.6% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.04x, net debt 4.66x normalized OE, 9.5 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path, key_numbers.md): 15% at $46.72 · 20% at $33.01 · 25% at $25.45. At $35.94 the stock clears 15% on the weighted path but not 20%.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.5 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above. The hybrid pre/post-deal nature of that TTM is disclosed under Owner's earnings and is a reason confidence is low, not medium.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 4.6%/yr): already credited via the growth adjustment in the blend (share count CAGR −4.56%, growth adj 4.56%, key_numbers.md); not double-counted. Note the pace has already slowed post-deal — H1 2026 buybacks were small while debt paydown takes priority — so the credited tailwind is a forward risk to the blend, one more reason the bull offsets were not stretched.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2025): found and named. 2023: net income −$6,655,000,000 vs OCF $4,335,000,000 — fundamentals.json shows discontinued operations of −$7,153,000,000 in 2023 (and −$17,324,000,000 in 2022) from the Worldpay Merchant Solutions held-for-sale write-downs, while operating income stayed positive ($1,447,000,000 in 2023). 2025: net income $382,000,000 vs continuing OCF $2,608,000,000 — the gap is mainly non-cash D&A of $1,883,000,000 (Worldpay-era intangible amortization added back in OCF) plus Worldpay equity-method items in net income, including the $108M contingent-consideration write-off triggered by the agreement to sell the remaining Worldpay stake (per the Q2 2026 results release). The OE base is OCF-based throughout, so neither divergence contaminates it.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 4.66x normalized OE): real, and the engine figure is stale in the bad direction. Balance sheet per the filing history (financials_history.csv, FY2025): total debt $13,082,000,000, cash $599,000,000, net debt $12,483,000,000, lease liabilities $249,000,000. That is BEFORE the Issuer Solutions close: post-deal reporting shows long-term debt of ~$15.4B at June 30, 2026 (up from $9.1B at end-2025) and H1 2026 net interest expense up 109% YoY, reflecting the ~$7.7B cash leg of the deal. The bear and super-bear cases (35% combined weight, OE multipliers 0.90/0.75) are the stress for this; the verdict is sized to them.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier C at 14.56% vs bull tier A at 22.10%): accepted — the verdict spans tiers, so the position logic follows the bear end: at the bear IV@15% of $34.71 the current $35.94 price is already fully valued. The weighted B is not a margin of safety against the bear case.
- **Basis break (not flagged in the final run, resolved here anyway):** three breaks — Worldpay consolidation (2019–2023 revenue mixes in merchant acquiring), the February 2024 deconsolidation (2024–25 on a continuing basis), and the January 2026 Issuer Solutions acquisition (2026 GAAP revenue +~30% YoY is the deal, pro forma +~5–6.5%). No CAGR in the blend is clean; growth was therefore anchored to the pro forma guidance range (4.5–5.0% for 2026) and the latest filed YoY (5.43%), as detailed in the sanity check above.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range: on the normalized (median) base of $4.33/share with the preliminary default scenarios, the engine printed a weighted IRR of 16.81% and IV@15% of $41.42 — also Tier B. On the TTM base with recalibrated scenarios it prints 18.62% / $46.72. Both defensible runs land in B; the disagreement is about how much headroom, not the tier. The bear end (C in both framings) is the sizing anchor.
- Quality is the debate, and the ROIC record settles it downward: this is a sticky, cash-generative processor (OE yield 14.19% at this price) that has earned below its cost of capital for a decade because it keeps overpaying for acquisitions. The Issuer deal is the third act of the same play — strategically coherent (issuing fits the banking base better than merchant acquiring did), but financed with debt at exactly the moment guidance was cut.
- The price already reflects a lot of failure: down ~46% YTD per market data, ~6x guided adjusted EPS of $6.15–6.24 — but adjusted EPS strips out the amortization and integration costs of the deal that produced the growth, and enterprise value is roughly double the market cap once the post-deal debt is counted. Cheap on equity multiples, not cheap on the whole capital structure.
- What would change the verdict: two clean post-deal years of OCF on the combined base (kills the hybrid-TTM problem), visible debt paydown from the claimed incremental free cash flow ($500M in 2026, $700M by 2028 per the closing release), and ROIC proxy finally clearing ~8%.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: B** (weighted IRR 18.62% on the TTM base; bear C 14.56% → bull A 22.10%; method range across the preliminary and final runs stays inside B)
- Confidence: **Low** (hybrid pre/post-deal TTM base, post-deal leverage not in the engine's net-debt figure, tier band spans C to A, 2026 guidance already cut once)
- One-liner: Sticky but low-return processor, moat 5/10 — clears 15% on the TTM base (18.6% weighted, IV $46.72 vs $35.94) but the band runs C to A, leverage stepped up again for Issuer Solutions, and 2026 pro forma guidance was already cut; size it like the bear end (C, 14.6%), not the weighted B.
